detail: The spleen distractor (my earlier factual_error) is gone. The distractors are now 'constantly forming tiny plugs that dissolve', 'stick to the wall but don't aggregate' and 'permanently glued to the vessel wall'. All three are clearly false and none is partly true.

The garbled sp-txa2 passage was replaced with two clean sentences: PGI2 from intact endothelium keeps platelets inactive, and TxA2 stimulates activation and aggregation. Together with the sp-hemostasis balance passage, they support the claim.

The sp-hemostasis 'within about 30 minutes... vascular spasm ensues' passage is removed. The OpenStax three-step passage now supports spasm-first. The remaining passages support adhesion, then activation, then aggregation.
The header-less table row is gone. The two dm-plavix passages and one sp-clopidogrel passage cleanly support both the 7–10 day lifetime block and recovery in about 5 days.

The text now explains the apparent contradiction: blocked platelets stay blocked for their 7–10 day life, and function returns gradually as new platelets are made, generally within about 5 days. A novice can follow it.

The first dm-effient passage is now complete ('...P2Y 12 class of ADP receptors on platelets'). The PMC table cells remain, but the header row (clopidogrel / prasugrel / ticagrelor) is now quoted, and a source_note explains the column order, so 'Irreversible Irreversible Reversible' can be tied to prasugrel. Acceptable.

The claim was deleted, so the citation problem is moot. The street point it was meant to carry ('spasm is temporary, so a controlled wound can re-bleed') is now missing from the module. That loss is tracked under ems-notes and does not block.
Rewritten. ADP, thrombin and TXA2 are now correctly attributed to other platelets and the clotting process, 'not from the wall itself'. Thrombin has a glossary entry.
Weibel-Palade bodies are explained inline as 'storage packets', and 'alpha granules' is covered by the new granule entry. Fine for an EMT-B.
'factor VIII' is now an alias of the clotting factor entry, so it is auto-underlined here, in c-vwd-2 and in q09#2.
The claim was deleted. 'Shear' no longer appears in any learner-facing text; it appears only in a c-gp2-2 source passage.
The granule entry now exists, and the text keeps the plain 'storage packets / small molecules' wording.
The text now names only P2Y12. P2Y1 was moved to a simplified note, with sources.
Arachidonic acid is explained inline ('a fat taken from the cell membrane'). It still does not say why 'always present' matters, but c-cox-2 carries that logic. Acceptable.
Fibrin, coagulation cascade and secondary hemostasis all have entries now. The direct-pressure street line was not added (see ems-notes).

Petechiae, purpura and mucosal are now glossed, which was the main concern. Still missing: the one-line contrast with the clotting-factor pattern (deep bleeding into joints and muscles). Only the q24#2 distractor hints at it. Non-blocking.
CYP2C19 is now explained inline ('a liver enzyme (mainly one called CYP2C19)'). The card front now tests why the drug needs the liver, not the enzyme name.

The claim text no longer says 'catalyze'. It now includes 'activated clotting factors act this way on the next factor', so the sp-coag-pathways passage is on-topic. 'catalyze' survives only inside a source quote.
The claim is now plain (calcium binds the factors and the platelet surface). Vitamin K, Gla domains and phosphatidylserine moved into the simplified note, with the fat explained inline.
Retitled to 'Match each platelet receptor to the job it does'. It no longer gives the answers away and no longer forces P2Y12 onto a 'step'.
Retitled around one concept: 'Predict the consequences of aspirin's irreversible COX-1 block'.
Its prereq m1-g07 itself requires m1-g02, so the GPIb contrast in q26#2 is covered through that chain. q27 was moved to g07.
The app excludes the pre-test from level counts and goal counters.

All three levels are present (recall 3, explain 6, apply 5, not counting the pretest), with 3 misconception goals and 3 cases. There is still no goal of its own for the skin and mucosal bleeding pattern (c-plug-2); it is tested only by q24#2 under g12. Non-blocking.
Still leaves out vascular spasm and adds 'Temporary platelet plug', so it does not test g01's four steps. The prompt was softened to 'platelet events', but the goal is unchanged. Non-blocking.
The distractors (activates fibrinogen, produces new platelets, dissolves old clots) are still obviously wrong. Non-blocking.
Normalization plus acceptance of the node's aliases covers GP-Ib, GPIB, GP 1b, glycoprotein 1b, GPIbα and similar. The lists no longer need to match across variants.

Normalization (slashes, hyphens, Greek, 'glycoprotein'→'GP', roman numerals) plus node aliases covers GP 2b/3a, GPIIbIIIa, GPIIb-IIIa, 2b/3a and αIIbβ3. Bare 'integrin' is still not accepted, which is fine.
The silly distractor 'Platelets have no receptors until they are 7 days old' is still there. Non-blocking.
Still orders 'GPIb' before 'Platelet', a part before its whole. Non-blocking.
Both now test g05 directly: the wall side (collagen) and the platelet side (GPIb).
Now framed around TXA2 as a recruitment signal, which ties the item to g06.
The explanation no longer says 'inside-out signaling'.
The true/false item became a one-word fill ('fibrin').
The nonsensical distractor 'Yes, but only if the count is above 500,000' is still there. 'Normal count, so it must be a clotting-factor problem' would be the realistic misconception. Non-blocking.

q19 was moved from g09 to g12, which fixes the g09 misalignment. All three variants are still recall (the 150,000 threshold and the word 'thrombocytopenia'), but g12 is an apply/case goal ('predict the bleeding at a cut'), so the mismatch has moved, not gone. Also, '150' (the way lab sheets print it) is still not accepted. The 'thrombocytopenea' misspelling is now covered by one-typo tolerance. Non-blocking.
The surgery-stop framing is gone. It now asks why yesterday's dose still matters, which implies no advice to stop a medicine.
'Tap the drug that permanently blocks COX-1' is still recall of the drug's identity under the apply goal g10. Non-blocking.
Normalization plus the node aliases cover P2Y12 variants.
Pure brand-name recall replaced with 'A med list says Plavix. Type the platelet receptor it blocks.' Acceptable for g11.
Now asks which step fails (adhesion), which matches g13.
q27 was reassigned to g07, and both variants test the GPIIb/IIIa–fibrinogen chain.
The items 'Activation' and 'GPIIb/IIIa activation' are still confusingly similar. Non-blocking.

Of the four points, only (4) is fixed (q20#2). Still missing: (1) the aspirin-for-suspected-ACS bridge on c-asa-1, the biggest relevance hook for an EMT-B; (2) the direct-pressure / re-bleed line (c-et-2, which would have carried it, was deleted, and c-plug-1 has no line); (3) the factor-bleed contrast on c-plug-2. Non-blocking.

Auto-underlining of every term and alias makes systematic [[ ]] markup unnecessary. I checked src/glossaryIndex.js: matching is case-insensitive and word-bounded (a hyphen counts as part of a word), so short aliases like 'IIa', 'Xa' and 'Va' do not fire inside 'GPIIb/IIIa', and 'reversible' does not fire inside 'irreversible'.

Entry added (g-gp-1).
Entry added (g-gran-1), with the degranulate/degranulation aliases.
Covered by the combined 'adhesion vs aggregation' entry (g-adag-1). A good choice for this learner, since the contrast is the point.
Entry added (g-act-1).
Entry added (g-hem-1), with primary and secondary as aliases.

Explained inline in c-cox-1 and its card. Either reword those three places ('from a membrane fat') or add an alias-style entry. Non-blocking.
Explained inline in c-vwf-2. Its use as a q06#1 distractor is fine now that the learner has met the term.

Still no entry. c-pc-1 and its card now say 'per microliter', but the bare '/µL' or 'per µL' remains in the m1-q19#1-3 prompts and explanations, the m1-q24#3 prompt and explanation, and the g-tcp-1 claim text. Suggest an entry 'µL (microliter)' with aliases 'µL' and 'microliter': 'A microliter is a millionth of a liter, roughly a tiny drop. Lab sheets often print the platelet count as 150–450, meaning thousands per µL.' This also helps the unaccepted '150' answer in q19.
Explained inline in c-clop-2.
Explained inline in c-plt-5 ('a loop that builds on itself'). c-txa2-1 and q12#1 explain the loop in their own words, and EMT A&P covers the term.
Entry added (g-rev-1).
Entry added (g-endo-1).
Entry added (g-sub-1).
Removed from learner-facing text (it remains only in a c-gp2-1 source quote).
Removed from the g-ca-1 claim. In the simplified note it is explained inline as 'a negatively charged fat'.
Removed from the g-ca-1 claim. It now appears only in the simplified note, which flags Module 2.
Removed from the claim text (it remains only in a source quote).
No entry. c-dg-2 states its vessel role plainly ('helps keep the vessel constricted'), which mostly answers the 'isn't that a brain chemical?' confusion. Low priority. Non-blocking.
Two sentences, EMT level, no undefined terms. The why_here maps each receptor to what it grabs, which is excellent. The claim text uses 'selectively binds', which is fine.
Two sentences, and it explains the 'GP' prefix, which is the useful part. The claim says 'carbohydrate (sugar)', which is self-glossed.
Two sentences, and it defines 'degranulates' in passing. The why_here says 'two main kinds' (there are three, counting lysosomal); 'main' covers it.
Two sentences, with the crisp wall-vs-each-other contrast. The why_here ties each step to its receptor. This is the best entry of the batch.
One sentence. All of its parts (granules, aggregation receptor) are themselves glossed or explained.
Two sentences that cover primary and secondary. The terms it uses (coagulation cascade, fibrin) have entries, and the chain stops there.
Clear and image-friendly ('thread-like', 'mesh'). The claim text says 'insoluble', which is acceptable vocabulary.
One sentence, accurate, and it forward-points to Module 2. The alias 'coagulation' will underline broadly, which is fine.

Accurate. The claim text uses 'prothrombin', which has no entry and is not explained (a scope-guard miss). The definition's '(activated factor II)' is fine because the clotting factor and 'a' suffix entries cover the numbering.
suggestion: Claim: 'Thrombin (factor IIa) is made from its inactive form, prothrombin (factor II), converts fibrinogen into fibrin, and activates platelets.'

detail: Two sentences, EMT level. It uses 'cofactor', which has an entry. 'Mostly made by the liver' is suitably hedged (vWF and factor VIII come partly from the endothelium).
Two sentences that capture exactly the duration logic g10 and g11 need. The why_here 'reversible but still lasts days' heads off the obvious misconception.
One plain sentence. The claim text's 'single-cell-layer lining' is fine.
Clear: 'under the endothelium', collagen-rich. 'Connective tissue' is EMT A&P vocabulary.
Accurate, with a size cutoff and non-blanching. Good street value. 'Mucous membranes' is underlined to the mucosal entry.

Accurate, and the ecchymosis = bruise line is useful. The claim text says 'non-blanching' twice. More importantly, 'ecchymosis' is aliased to the purpura entry, so tapping 'ecchymosis' opens a page headed 'purpura'. The definition does cover it, so this is minor.
suggestion: Claim: 'Purpura are non-blanching spots larger than 2 mm.' Keep or drop the ecchymosis alias; either is acceptable.

detail: A practical list of examples. 'Epistaxis' in the claim text is self-glossed by its placement. The 'mucous membranes' alias sends the learner to the bleeding entry rather than an anatomy definition, which is acceptable in this context.
One sentence, and the definition writes 'per microliter' out in full. The claim text uses '/µL' (see the µL glossary_needed item).
All three levels are present: recall (g01–g03), explain (g04–g09), apply (g10–g14). The pretest is excluded from counts.

Every goal has questions, and they test it: g01 q01/q02; g02 q03–q05; g03 q06/q07; g04 q08/q09; g05 q10/q11; g06 q12/q13; g07 q14/q15/q27; g08 q16/q17; g09 q18; g10 q20/q21; g11 q22/q23; g12 q19/q24; g13 q25; g14 q26. Remaining soft spots are single variants or one recall item under an apply goal (q01#3, q19, q21#3), listed above as still_open. No goal is untested or tested only off-target, since each has at least one fully aligned question (g12 through q24).
